---
title: "Computational genomics"
subtitle: "One question, reproducible answers—from a laptop to an HPC cluster"
---

## Sequence data do not interpret themselves

A FASTQ record describes a sequence and a base-quality encoding. A genomic coordinate is meaningful only with a reference assembly. A computational pipeline is reproducible only when its inputs, references, versions, parameters and execution environment can be reconstructed.

### Foundations

Terminal navigation, Bash, Python and R; compressed files and checksums; FASTQ, BAM/CRAM, BED, bigWig and VCF formats; genomic coordinates and reference builds; Git and sample metadata.

### Beyond the laptop

High-performance computing with job schedulers, computational resource estimates, software environments, command-line logging, batch processing and workflow managers. A useful first exercise asks students to execute **the same logic** locally and on a cluster and compare provenance.

### From sequencing to biological inference

Read alignment and filtering; assay-specific QC; bulk and single-cell chromatin accessibility; differential analysis; genomic intervals, peak calling, single-cell integration and 3D genome interpretation. Multiple approaches may produce different but superficially plausible biological narratives.
